target_concept: Define and interpret the mean of the latent Gaussian distribution in a VAE.

mcq.questionText: In a variational autoencoder, what does the mean (μ) of the latent Gaussian distribution represent?
options: The average latent code that captures the central tendency of the encoded data
The spread or variability of the latent codes around the average
A deterministic point that the decoder reconstructs without any randomness
The weight matrix used in the encoder network to map inputs to latent space
mcq.correctAnswer: The average latent code that captures the central tendency of the encoded data
mcq.explanation: The mean (μ) of the latent Gaussian distribution specifies the central location of that distribution, i.e., the average latent representation for a given input. It reflects the central tendency, while variance describes the spread. It is not a deterministic point nor a network weight.
